newsitem.title: FRANCE: RALLYING-KLEINSCHMIDT FIRST WOMAN TO WIN DAKAR STAGE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-KLEINSCHMIDT FIRST WOMAN TO WIN DAKAR STAGE.

text.p: Jutta Kleinschmidt made Dakar Rally history on Monday when she became the first woman to win a stage.
The German, driving a Buggy, took advantage of the struggle between Mitsubishi's leading trio of drivers to win the 315 km ninth section between Agadez and Oclan in Niger.
"What she did is fantastic, the more so as it's a fine reply to all those who doubted her abilities," said Buggy team leader Jean-Louis Schlesser, who retired from the event last week.
Despite the win, Kleinschmidt posed no threat for the Mitsubishi team in the overall standings. She was sixth overall, 4-1/2 hours behind leader Jean-Pierre Fontenay.
The Frenchman took first place from Mitsubishi team mate Kenjiro Shinozuka of Japan by a mere 17 seconds. Fellow Frenchman Bruno Saby was third, eight minutes six seconds behind Fontenay.
Frenchman Thierry Magnaldi had a perfect day in the motorcycle section. The KTM rider won his second stage, ahead of the Yamahas of compatriots David Castera and Stephane Peterhansel.
Peterhansel still led overall by a comfortable one hour 27 minutes margin lead over Spain's Jordi Arcarons.
The stages on Tuesday and Wednesday are long "marathon" runs held without mechanical assistance and may lead to surprises.
